Injection 2 already achieved the maximum CRF; shorten its gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keeping temperature and solvent endpoints fixed isolates the slope effect on the critical early pair, whose R of 2.25 provides some margin.

Shorten the fully resolved method from injection 9 by one more grid step while holding temperature and solvent endpoints fixed. This tests the fastest gradient boundary for the critical early pair; injection 9 remains a maximum-CRF fallback.

Lower temperature while retaining the fast gradient to test whether temperature selectivity restores the early pair to R ≥ 1.5. The last peak at 3.97 min leaves ample time margin for the increased retention.

Test the minimum gradient duration, using lower temperature to improve early-pair selectivity and a slightly narrower solvent window to moderate compression. Injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved fallback.

Reduce phi1 by one grid step to make the gradient slightly shallower and lift the early pair above its near-threshold R of 1.49. The last peak may elute later during the hold, but its current 3.18 min retention leaves ample margin below 10 min.

Shift injection 13's solvent window upward while preserving its gradient slope, aiming to accelerate the late hold peak without losing early-pair resolution. This tests whether the higher starting organic fraction retains enough separation to keep the maximum CRF.

Shift both solvent endpoints upward by another grid step, preserving the slope that resolved every pair in injection 14. The stronger final solvent should accelerate the last peak; monitor the early pair for loss of retention and resolution.

Shift the solvent window upward one more step while preserving gradient slope, aiming to shorten the last peak's retention while maintaining CRF 1.000. The early pair remains critical, but its resolution has held near 1.6 over the preceding window shifts.

Raise phi0 one grid step with phi1 already at its maximum to test a shorter fully resolved elution window. The shallower slope may help the critical early pair, but its proximity to the solvent front makes this a useful boundary test.

Raise temperature one grid step to shorten the fastest confirmed fully resolved method while keeping the solvent window fixed. The critical early pair has R 1.77, providing some margin to test the temperature-driven loss of selectivity.

Test a narrower, higher-starting solvent window at the temperature that favors early-pair selectivity. This probes whether further window trimming can preserve full resolution before the early peaks become too weakly retained; injection 18 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Return to the resolved starting fraction and test one temperature step above injection 18 to establish the speed–resolution boundary. The early pair may fall below 1.5, in which case injection 18 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Back off to the fully resolved temperature and lower phi1 one step to improve the critical pair's resolution margin through a shallower gradient. This seeks a more robust maximum-CRF alternative to injection 18, accepting a modest increase in last-peak retention.

Test a robustness-focused alternative using lower temperature and a lower starting organic fraction to keep the critical pair farther from the solvent front. The shallower slope than injection 16 should improve resolution margin while retaining a short run and maximum CRF.

Lower injection 21's temperature one step to improve the critical early pair's selectivity while preserving the minimum gradient duration. This tests a higher-resolution-margin alternative expected to retain maximum CRF with the last peak near 2.8 min.

Raise injection 22's temperature one step to shorten retention while testing whether its early-pair resolution margin remains sufficient. This also checks a lower-starting-organic alternative to injection 21, with the early peaks farther from the solvent front.

Use the final injection to test a higher-resolution-margin alternative: narrow injection 22's solvent window one step while retaining its favorable temperature and early-peak retention. This should preserve maximum CRF with a modest time increase; injection 18 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
